faqs.a: A valid format means the code matches the country's pattern — it does not prove the code exists or that mail will reach it. A six-digit Indian PIN like 999999 matches the pattern but may not be a real PIN. For existence checks, use the country's postal service lookup.
faqs.q: Does valid mean the code really exists?

faqs.a: The UAE has never operated a public postal-code system; mail is delivered to PO boxes instead. So any 'UAE postal code' you see in a form is either the PO box number or made up. This tool tells you that directly instead of pretending to validate it.
faqs.q: Why does the UAE show as not used?

faqs.a: Yes — the US ZIP+4 format (five digits, hyphen, four digits, like 90210-1234) is accepted alongside the plain five-digit ZIP. Both are official US formats.
No. British postcodes mix letters and digits (for example, SW1A 1AA), so the check is case-insensitive and allows the optional space. Typing sw1a1aa is just as valid as SW1A 1AA.
faqs.q: Do UK postcodes have to be uppercase?

faqs.a: Yes. Indian PIN codes are six digits and the first digit is never 0 — it runs 1–9 by postal region. Codes like 012345 are rejected by this tool, matching India Post's own numbering.
faqs.q: Why do Indian PIN codes reject a leading zero?

faqs.a: Correct. Japan's 7-digit codes are written with a hyphen after the third digit (100-0001), and the hyphen is required here. Brazil accepts the hyphen as optional (01310100 and 01310-100 both pass).
faqs.q: Is the hyphen required in Japanese codes?

zip-code-format-validator.formula:
Validation is pattern matching with regular expressions — there is no arithmetic.
India: ^[1-9][0-9]{5}$  (6 digits, first 1–9)
USA: ^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$  (ZIP or ZIP+4)
UK: ^[A-Z]{1,2}[0-9][A-Z0-9]?\s?[0-9][A-Z]{2}$  (case-insensitive)
Japan: ^\d{3}-\d{4}$  (hyphen required)

keyFacts: Postal-code formats differ by country — there is no universal pattern.
India uses 6-digit PIN codes; the first digit is never 0.
The US uses 5-digit ZIP codes, optionally ZIP+4.
The UK and Canada mix letters and digits in their codes.
The UAE has no public postal-code system at all.
This tool checks format only, not whether a code is real.

zip-code-format-validator.quickAnswer: Postal codes follow strict national patterns, and this tool checks your code against the right one. India's PIN is 6 digits starting 1–9, so 500001 is valid; the US accepts 90210 and 90210-1234; Japan needs 100-0001 with the hyphen. Pick a country, type the code, and get an instant valid/invalid verdict — including honest handling of the UAE, which has no postal codes at all.

zip-code-format-validator.workedExample:
India, code 500001:
1. Pattern: ^[1-9][0-9]{5}$ — 6 digits, first digit 1–9.
2. 500001 has 6 digits and starts with 5.
3. Verdict: valid.
Counter-example: 050001 fails because the first digit is 0.
USA, code 90210-1234: matches ^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$ → valid (ZIP+4).
